turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - b3_te_zt400_train.csv: 300 real samples, columns process/composition
    columns (Sb, O, Te, Mg, Se, Co, Sn, Pb, S, Si, Cu, Ni, Ge, Bi, Ti, Fe,
    Zn, Zr, In, Ca, Ag) and `target` (the measured zT (thermoelectric figure
    of merit) at 400 K).
  - b3_te_zt400_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE samples whose zT (thermoelectric
    figure of merit) at 400 K was NOT measured, columns `candidate_id` and
    the same process/composition columns.

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the HIGHEST zT
(thermoelectric figure of merit) at 400 K, then select the 5 best candidates
from the pool.

Reason from the training data, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training compositions with the largest measured zT at 400 K belong to a small number of well-known thermoelectric families (Pb-deficient PbTe, Mg3Sb2-type Zintls, Mg2(Si,Sn), In-filled CoSb3 skutterudites, and a near-pure-Sn point). Direct composition-space nearest-neighbor matching of the 100 unlabeled candidates against those high-zT exemplars yields a clear ranking:

- c037 is essentially identical to the Pb0.45Te0.5 sample (zT = 0.78).
- c010 is essentially identical to the Sn0.56 sample (zT = 0.71).
- c043 differs from the highest Mg3Sb2-type point (zT = 0.79) only by the absence of a 2 at.% Co substitution.
- c046 is the Sn-rich Mg2(Si,Sn) analogue of the zT = 0.66 Mg2(Sn,Ge) point.
- c096 is the lightly In-filled CoSb3 analogue of the zT = 0.70 filled-skutterudite point.

All other pool entries lie appreciably farther from any training point whose zT exceeds 0.55 and are therefore ranked lower.

Final: c037, c010, c043, c046, c096
